words.def: Rain is water that falls from the clouds in little drops.
ask: What do you like to do on a rainy day?
words.sentence: The rain fell on the tin roof all night.
words.adultDef: Rain is water that falls from the clouds in drops. Plants and animals need rain to drink and grow. When it rains, we might grab an umbrella – or splash in the puddles!

words.def: To aim is to point something at a target, like aiming a ball at the goal.
ask: What do you aim at when you play a game?
words.sentence: Take aim and kick the footy between the posts.
words.adultDef: To aim means to point something at the thing you want to hit – like a ball at the goal or a beanbag at a bucket. When you take aim, you look carefully before you throw or kick.

words.def: Pain is the hurt feeling you get when you bump your knee.
ask: What do you do when you have a pain, like a sore knee?
words.sentence: I had a pain in my knee after I fell off my scooter.
words.adultDef: Pain is the hurt feeling you get when part of your body is sore – like when you fall over and graze your knee, or have a toothache. A band-aid or a cuddle can help it feel better.

words.def: To wait is to stay where you are until something happens, like waiting in line.
ask: What is something you have to wait for?
words.sentence: We had to wait in line for a sausage at the footy.
words.adultDef: To wait means to stay where you are until something happens. We wait for the bus, wait in line at the canteen and wait for our turn in a game.

words.def: May is a polite word we use to ask for something, like: May I have a turn, please?
ask: How do you ask nicely if you want a turn?
words.sentence: May I have a turn on the swing, please?
words.adultDef: We say may when we ask nicely if we are allowed to do something: "May I have a turn?" It can also mean something might happen: "It may rain today." (May with a capital M is also a month of the year!)

words.def: A day is the time from sunrise to sunset. There are seven days in a week.
ask: What is your favourite day of the week?
words.sentence: It was a hot, sunny day at the beach.
words.adultDef: A day is the time from when the sun comes up in the morning until it goes down at night, when it is light outside. There are seven days in a week.

words.def: A way is a path or direction, like the way to school. It can also mean how you do something.
ask: Do you know the way from your house to school?
words.sentence: Mum showed me the way to the new library.
words.adultDef: The way is the road or path you take to get somewhere: "Which way to the beach?" Way can also mean how you do something: "This is the way I tie my shoes."

words.def: To lay is to put something down flat, like laying a towel on the sand. Chickens lay eggs!
ask: What animals do you know that lay eggs?
words.sentence: Our chooks lay eggs every morning.
words.adultDef: To lay means to put something down flat, or to make an egg come out. Hens (chooks!) lay eggs. We lay a picnic rug on the grass and lay the table for dinner.
